lessons.title: 1. Pass-by-Reference (&)
lessons.description: In C++, pass-by-reference (`type&`) allows functions to modify caller variables efficiently. Implement `swap(int& a, int& b)`.
learning_objectives: Use C++ reference parameters & to mutate values

tests.name: test_swap
tests.test_code: int x = 5, y = 10; swap_ints(x, y); assert(x == 10 && y == 5);

source.name: cppreference.com — References — 'Declares a named variable as a reference'

lessons.title: 2. Const References (const &)
lessons.description: Pass large objects by `const &` to avoid expensive copies while guaranteeing immutability. Implement `greeting(const std::string& name)` returning `"Hello, "` followed by the name and a `!`.
learning_objectives: Pass parameters by const std::string& in C++

source.name: cppreference.com — References — const reference function parameters

exercises.question: This lesson passes large objects by `const &` to avoid a copy while guaranteeing the function cannot change them. Select every parameter declaration that does both.
exercises.explanation: `const &` borrows without copying and forbids writes. Plain `std::string` copies, and a non-const reference can modify the caller's object.

lessons.title: 3. In-Place Range Clamping (Concept Challenge)
lessons.description: Clamp a double variable in-place using reference.
learning_objectives: Clamp values in-place using reference parameters

source.name: cppreference.com — References — modifying the referred object

lessons.title: 4. Value Incrementer (Practice)
lessons.description: Practice with pass-by-reference: implement increment(int& value, int amount = 1) so it adds amount to value in-place; the caller's variable must change. The test runs increment(val, 5) on val == 10 and asserts val == 15.
